w10:3: This week's map — from living religion, through the Adjuster and the soul, to prayer and worship and the God of time
w10:6: If the last two weeks told the outer history of our planet, this week turns to the inner history of a human being. The Urantia Book says that true religion is not an institution or a creed but a personal experience of knowing God as Father. That experience is possible because the Universal Father has sent a fragment of Himself, the Thought Adjuster, to live in the human mind. As mind and Adjuster work together, a soul grows that can survive death, and it grows through prayer, worship, and love of our neighbors. All these small growths are added to the God who is Himself growing in time, the Supreme Being.
w10:11: Picture an old radio. The station broadcasts day and night, but if the dial is slightly off, all that comes through is static. Turn the dial slowly with a fingertip, and at the moment the frequency lines up, a song rises clear out of the crackle. The signal had filled the room all along. What changed was the receiver.
w10:13: The inner story told in The Urantia Book is much like this. God is present in each human mind at this very moment, leading without pause, yet most of the time we miss the music.
w10:15: This week looks at that inner station, the Thought Adjuster; at the soul that grows as it receives the signal; and at prayer and worship, the practice of tuning the dial.
w10:21: The word "religion" usually brings to mind buildings, ceremonies, and doctrines. The Urantia Book reverses the order: the root of religion is the living relationship between one person and God. Paper 99 puts it in a single sentence.

w10:23.q: Always keep in mind: True religion is to know God as your Father and man as your brother. Religion is not a slavish belief in threats of punishment or magical promises of future mystical rewards.

w10:25: Where does this experience take place? Paper 101 answers: not in stirred-up emotion, but in the highest kind of thinking.

w10:27.q: Religion is not the product of reason, but viewed from within, it is altogether reasonable. Religion is not derived from the logic of human philosophy, but as a mortal experience it is altogether logical.

w10:29.q: The divine spirit makes contact with mortal man, not by feelings or emotions, but in the realm of the highest and most spiritualized thinking. It is your thoughts, not your feelings, that lead you Godward.

w10:31: The intensity of a feeling is not the measure of a religious experience. God meets people in the quiet place where they think about what is right and choose it.
w10:35: The book draws a careful line between belief and faith. Accepting a teaching as true is belief; it becomes faith only when it actually changes the direction of a life.

w10:37.q: Belief has attained the level of faith when it motivates life and shapes the mode of living. The acceptance of a teaching as true is not faith; that is mere belief.

w10:39.q: Belief is always limiting and binding; faith is expanding and releasing. Belief fixates, faith liberates. … Beliefs may become group possessions, but faith must be personal.

w10:41: Belief and faith (the author's summary, based on 101:8.1–2)
w10:44: That belief governing the way one lives
w10:46: Can be held by a group
Grows only in the individual heart
w10:49: A creed can be recited together, but no one can have faith on someone else's behalf. What, then, unites people of faith?

w10:51.q: Someday religionists will get together and actually effect co-operation on the basis of unity of ideals and purposes rather than attempting to do so on the basis of psychological opinions and theological beliefs. Goals rather than creeds should unify religionists.

w10:53: Paper 103 makes the order of theology and religion plain.

w10:55.q: It is much easier for men to agree on religious values—goals—than on beliefs—interpretations. … Theology does not produce religion; it is religion that produces theologic philosophy.

w10:59: None of this means the book regards religious groups as useless. People who share a faith naturally gather, and Paper 99 describes warmly what such a gathering is for.

w10:61.q: There is a real purpose in the socialization of religion. It is the purpose of group religious activities to dramatize the loyalties of religion; to magnify the lures of truth, beauty, and goodness; … to enhance the service of unselfish fellowship; to glorify the potentials of family life; to promote religious education; to provide wise counsel and spiritual guidance; and to encourage group worship.

w10:63: The danger comes when the gathering stiffens into an institution. The same section goes on to give a long list of warnings.

w10:65.q: But as religion becomes institutionalized, its power for good is curtailed, while the possibilities for evil are greatly multiplied. The dangers of formalized religion are: fixation of beliefs and crystallization of sentiments; … diversion of religion from the service of God to the service of the church; inclination of leaders to become administrators instead of ministers; … and gradually loses the saving message of the gospel of eternal salvation.

w10:67: And it leaves one short, solid sentence.

w10:69.q: Sectarianism is a disease of institutional religion, and dogmatism is an enslavement of the spiritual nature. It is far better to have a religion without a church than a church without religion.

w10:71: Living religion and a hardened institution (the author's summary, based on 99:5–6)
w10:78: Fruits of the spirit, brotherly love
w10:81: **A common misunderstanding**: The Urantia Book rejects the church and teaches people to believe on their own.
w10:82: **What The Urantia Book says**: Religious groups have real purposes: worship and education, fellowship and service (99:6.2). What the book warns against is creedal pressure and institutional rigidity. Paper 103 says there is great hope for any church that frees its members from the pressure of creeds (103:5.12).
w10:85: 2. The Thought Adjuster, a Fragment of the Father
w10:87: Farthest Away and Nearest of All
w10:89: In Week 1 we briefly met the phrase "a fragment of God." Paper 107 introduces this fragment in full, and it opens with a striking paradox.

w10:91.q: Although the Universal Father is personally resident on Paradise, at the very center of the universes, he is also actually present on the worlds of space in the minds of his countless children of time, for he indwells them as the Mystery Monitors. The eternal Father is at one and the same time farthest removed from, and most intimately associated with, his planetary mortal sons.

w10:93: "Mystery Monitor" is another name for the Thought Adjuster, and to "indwell" is to live within. The Father at the center of all things is at the same time inside each human mind. Why would He do this? Paper 107 links the gift to the command we saw in Paper 1: "Be you perfect."

w10:95.q: God, having commanded man to be perfect, even as he is perfect, has descended as the Adjuster to become man's experiential partner in the achievement of the supernal destiny which has been thus ordained. The fragment of God which indwells the mind of man is the absolute and unqualified assurance that man can find the Universal Father in association with this divine Adjuster

w10:97: God did not only give the command; He came down Himself to be our partner in keeping it. Is the Adjuster, then, something like an angel that God created? Paper 107 says no.

w10:99.q: All are agreed that they proceed direct from the Universal Father, the First Source and Center. They are not created beings; they are fragmentized entities constituting the factual presence of the infinite God. … they are of God, and as far as we are able to discern, they are God.

w10:101: The Adjuster is not a messenger God sends but a piece of God Himself. A cup of seawater is not the whole ocean, yet it is the very same water. Paper 107 compares the Adjuster's work to a compass.

w10:103.q: The Adjuster is an absolute essence of an infinite being imprisoned within the mind of a finite creature … The Adjuster is the divine universe reality which factualizes the truth that God is man's Father. The Adjuster is man's infallible cosmic compass, always and unerringly pointing the soul Godward.

w10:105: To call God our Father is therefore no mere figure of speech. The Father has actually shared His own spirit with His children. And this guide never fails.

w10:107.q: Angels and other high types of spirit beings, not excepting the local universe type of Sons, may occasionally embrace evil, may sometimes depart from the divine way, but Adjusters never falter. They are absolutely dependable, and this is equally true of all seven groups.

w10:111: The Adjuster is not here to make life comfortable. Paper 108 is clear on this point.

w10:113.q: Their mission chiefly concerns the future life, not this life. They are called heavenly helpers, not earthly helpers. They are not interested in making the mortal career easy; rather are they concerned in making your life reasonably difficult and rugged, so that decisions will be stimulated and multiplied.

w10:115: A good coach does not make an athlete's day easy. The Adjuster also takes pleasure in our health and happiness (110:1.3), but all of that care gathers toward one end: that we survive forever and grow more and more like God.
w10:117: The trouble is that this leading is hard to hear.

w10:119.q: But usually, when your Adjuster attempts to communicate with you, the message is lost in the material currents of the energy streams of human mind; only occasionally do you catch an echo, a faint and distant echo, of the divine voice.

w10:121: This is exactly the radio of the opening story. Does that mean someone who hears poorly has failed?

w10:123.q: Ignorance alone can never prevent survival; neither can confusional doubts nor fearful uncertainty. Only conscious resistance to the Adjuster's leading can prevent the survival of the evolving immortal soul.

w10:125: Doubting and wandering are quite different from deliberately turning away. Co-operating with the Adjuster is not a matter of special mystical experiences; it happens in everyday motives and decisions (110:3.6). Nor is it a gloomy self-denial.

w10:127.q: The great goal of human existence is to attune to the divinity of the indwelling Adjuster; … But a devoted and determined effort to realize eternal destiny is wholly compatible with a lighthearted and joyous life and with a successful and honorable career on earth. … the ideal life is one of loving service rather than an existence of fearful apprehension.

w10:131: Paper 107 also mentions an intriguing detail: the Adjuster is called by different names as a person grows older.

w10:133.q: From the arrival of the Adjuster to comparative full growth, about twenty years of age on Urantia, the Monitors are sometimes designated Thought Changers. From this time to the attainment of the age of discretion, about forty years, the Mystery Monitors are called Thought Adjusters. From the attainment of discretion to deliverance from the flesh, they are often referred to as Thought Controllers.

w10:135: The Adjuster arrives around the time a child makes the first moral decision, on average just before the sixth birthday (108:2.1). The three names can be read not as a change in the Adjuster but as a deepening relationship between the person and the Adjuster.
w10:137: After telling the whole life of Jesus, the very last paper of the book leaves this task to the people of today.

w10:139.q: The great challenge to modern man is to achieve better communication with the divine Monitor that dwells within the human mind.

w10:141: Three names across a lifetime — Thought Changer, Thought Adjuster, Thought Controller (the author's summary, based on 107:0.7 and 108:2.1)
w10:144: **Mystery Monitor**: Another name for the Thought Adjuster, so called because its nature is still veiled in mystery.
w10:145: **Indwelling**: Living within. The Adjuster indwells the human mind, not the brain (110:1.1).
w10:146: **Fusion**: The eternal union of a surviving human soul with the Adjuster. Once fused, the two can never again be separated.
w10:150: **A common misunderstanding**: The Thought Adjuster is just another name for conscience, or for the good thoughts in my own mind.
w10:151: **What The Urantia Book says**: The Adjuster is neither a created being nor part of the human mind; it is a fragment of God Himself (107:1.2). It never overrides the human will but always respects a person's choices (111:1.8), and it works in the conflicts between right and wrong even when the person is not aware of it (108:5.9).
w10:158: The Adjuster works in the human mind. Paper 111 traces where each of three things comes from: the body, the Adjuster, and the mind.

w10:160.q: Material evolution has provided you a life machine, your body; the Father himself has endowed you with the purest spirit reality known in the universe, your Thought Adjuster. But into your hands, subject to your own decisions, has been given mind, and it is by mind that you live or die. It is within this mind and with this mind that you make those moral decisions which enable you to achieve Adjusterlikeness, and that is Godlikeness.

w10:162: Evolution gave the body, and the Father gave the Adjuster. Only the mind, standing between them, is placed "into your hands." Paper 111 pictures the three as a single ship.

w10:164.q: Mind is your ship, the Adjuster is your pilot, the human will is captain. The master of the mortal vessel should have the wisdom to trust the divine pilot to guide the ascending soul into the morontia harbors of eternal survival.

w10:166: However skilled the pilot, the captain is the one in command. The Adjuster shows the way, but it is the human will that sets the course. Paper 111 stresses the point again.

w10:168.q: The Adjusters manipulate but never dominate man's mind against his will; to the Adjusters the human will is supreme.

w10:172: What, then, is the soul? The Urantia Book says the soul is not handed to us at the start; it grows.

w10:174.q: There are three and not two factors in the evolutionary creation of such an immortal soul. These three antecedents of the morontia human soul are: 1. The human mind and all cosmic influences antecedent thereto and impinging thereon. 2. The divine spirit indwelling this human mind … 3. The relationship between material mind and divine spirit, which connotes a value and carries a meaning not found in either of the contributing factors to such an association. The reality of this unique relationship is neither material nor spiritual but morontial. It is the soul.

w10:176: The soul is born of the relationship between mind and Adjuster. When two people share a long friendship, the friendship becomes a new reality that belongs to neither one alone but lives between them. Paper 112 calls the soul a "child."

w10:178.q: There is something real, something of human evolution, something additional to the Mystery Monitor, which survives death. This newly appearing entity is the soul, and it survives the death of both your physical body and your material mind. This entity is the conjoint child of the combined life and efforts of the human you in liaison with the divine you, the Adjuster.

w10:180: How the soul is born — the morontia soul growing out of the relationship between mind and Adjuster (the author's summary, based on 111:1.9, 111:2.4–7 and 112:5.12)
w10:184: What makes the soul grow? Paper 111 looks less at how much a mind knows than at which way it faces.

w10:186.q: And it is not so much what mind comprehends as what mind desires to comprehend that insures survival; it is not so much what mind is like as what mind is striving to be like that constitutes spirit identification. … What you are today is not so important as what you are becoming day by day and in eternity.

w10:188: Even with much still unknown and much still lacking, the soul grows as long as it keeps choosing the direction of wanting to know God. And what grows in this way is not lost.

w10:190.q: But it is forever true: What you begin in time you will assuredly finish in eternity—if it is worth finishing.

w10:192: The Personality That Does Not Change
w10:194: Paper 112 tells us where this journey begins.

w10:196.q: Urantia is your starting point; here you and your divine Thought Adjuster are joined in temporary union. You have been endowed with a perfect guide; … And throughout all of these successive ages and stages of evolutionary growth, there is one part of you that remains absolutely unaltered, and that is personality—permanence in the presence of change.

w10:198: What stays the same while the soul grows is personality. Personality is the unique selfhood the Universal Father gives each person, and no two are alike (112:0.12). It is this same "I" that awakens on the mansion worlds after death. There the Adjuster returns and links the old life with the new.

w10:200.q: The Thought Adjuster will recall and rehearse for you only those memories and experiences which are a part of, and essential to, your universe career. … But personality and the relationships between personalities are never scaffolding; mortal memory of personality relationships has cosmic value and will persist.

w10:202: Many memories are cleared away like scaffolding once the building is finished, but our relationships with the people we loved remain. The journey after death that we followed in Week 6 has its seed growing here and now, on this earth.
w10:205: **Soul**: The morontia reality born and growing out of the relationship between the mind and the indwelling Adjuster. It survives death.
w10:206: **Morontia**: The level of reality between the material and the spiritual. The soul and the bodies of the mansion worlds belong to it.
w10:207: **Personality**: The unique endowment the Universal Father gives each person, the "I" that remains unchanged in the midst of change.
w10:214: Paper 100 sums up the path of spiritual growth in three steps.

w10:216.q: Spiritual growth is first an awakening to needs, next a discernment of meanings, and then a discovery of values. The evidence of true spiritual development consists in the exhibition of a human personality motivated by love, activated by unselfish ministry, and dominated by the wholehearted worship of the perfection ideals of divinity.

w10:218: We realize that something is missing, we begin to see what the events of life mean, and among them we discover what is truly precious. This growth is not always smooth.

w10:220.q: Religious perplexities are inevitable; there can be no growth without psychic conflict and spiritual agitation.

w10:222: A season when faith is shaken need not be seen as failure. Paper 100 says there is a place that does not fall even in such times.

w10:224.q: Jesus portrayed the profound surety of the God-knowing mortal when he said: "To a God-knowing kingdom believer, what does it matter if all things earthly crash?" Temporal securities are vulnerable, but spiritual sureties are impregnable. When the flood tides of human adversity, selfishness, cruelty, hate, malice, and jealousy beat about the mortal soul, you may rest in the assurance that there is one inner bastion, the citadel of the spirit, which is absolutely unassailable

w10:226: The stairway of spiritual growth — from an awakening to needs to a discovery of values (the author's summary, based on 100:2.2 and 100:4.2)
w10:230: The evidence of growth is love. Yet love does not come from resolve alone. Paper 100 offers a very practical path.

w10:232.q: You cannot truly love your fellows by a mere act of the will. Love is only born of thoroughgoing understanding of your neighbor's motives and sentiments. It is not so important to love all men today as it is that each day you learn to love one more human being.

w10:234: Paper 100 also traces how understanding ripens into love.

w10:236.q: If once you understand your neighbor, you will become tolerant, and this tolerance will grow into friendship and ripen into love.

w10:238: Trying to understand the one person who weighs on our mind today is a bigger step than vowing to love all of humanity.
w10:240: Prayer Changes the One Who Prays
w10:242: What is prayer? Paper 91 sets prayer beside magic to show the difference.

w10:244.q: Magic was an attempt to adjust Deity to conditions; prayer is the effort to adjust the personality to the will of Deity.

w10:246: Magic tries to bend heaven to our will; prayer tries to bend our will to heaven. Paper 91 compares this to a bird's wings.

w10:248.q: But real praying does attain reality. Even when the air currents are ascending, no bird can soar except by outstretched wings. Prayer elevates man because it is a technique of progressing by the utilization of the ascending spiritual currents of the universe.

w10:250.q: God answers man's prayer by giving him an increased revelation of truth, an enhanced appreciation of beauty, and an augmented concept of goodness. Prayer is a subjective gesture, but it contacts with mighty objective realities on the spiritual levels of human experience

w10:252.q: Prayer is not a technique of escape from conflict but rather a stimulus to growth in the very face of conflict. Pray only for values, not things; for growth, not for gratification.

w10:254: Jesus, too, taught his disciples at length about prayer at Jotapata, a small town in Galilee. One of his main points was this.

w10:256.q: Prayer does not change the divine attitude toward man, but it does change man's attitude toward the changeless Father.

w10:258: He also taught them to be silent for a while after praying.

w10:260.q: Jesus taught his followers that, when they had made their prayers to the Father, they should remain for a time in silent receptivity to afford the indwelling spirit the better opportunity to speak to the listening soul. … Worship, taught Jesus, makes one increasingly like the being who is worshiped.

w10:262: If prayer is the time for speaking, silence is the time for listening, the time for tuning the radio dial. As prayer matures, it becomes worship. Prayer still carries something of our own needs; worship asks for nothing and simply delights in God for being God.
w10:266: All this growth comes down to one choice: the choice to do the Father's will. Paper 111 says this choice does not crush the will but uses it most fully.

w10:268.q: This choosing does not so much consist in the negation of creature will—"Not my will but yours be done"—as it consists in the creature's positive affirmation: "It is my will that your will be done."

w10:271: Paul asked, "Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?" (1 Corinthians 3:16). Jesus taught his hearers to enter into the closet and pray to the Father "which is in secret" (Matthew 6:6). The Urantia Book explains this "God within" more fully under the name of the Thought Adjuster.
w10:275: **A common misunderstanding**: Prayer is a way of getting what we want, and if we ask long and hard enough, God will change His mind.
w10:276: **What The Urantia Book says**: Prayer changes not God's attitude but ours (146:2.8). God answers the attitude of the soul, not the words (91:8.12). Jesus warned against the habit of praying only in times of trouble, and taught that the one form of prayer suited to all God's children is "Your will be done" (146:2.12).
w10:279: 5. God in Time, the Supreme Being
w10:283: Last of all we meet the least familiar idea of the week. God the Father is eternal and perfect, and He does not grow. Yet The Urantia Book says there is also a God who grows along with the universes of time and space. He is the Supreme Being.

w10:285.q: The Supreme is God-in-time; his is the secret of creature growth in time; his also is the conquest of the incomplete present and the consummation of the perfecting future.

w10:287: "The Supreme" is the book's shorter name for the Supreme Being. Paper 116 observes that an honest look at confused Urantia makes it reasonable to conclude that this world is governed by Creators who are not yet perfect (116:0.2). The universe is not a finished house but a house still being built.
w10:291: The most remarkable thing about this teaching is that human choices really are added to that growth.

w10:293.q: To the extent that we do the will of God in whatever universe station we may have our existence, in that measure the almighty potential of the Supreme becomes one step more actual.

w10:295: Paper 115 briefly shows how our standing differs before the Father and before the Supreme.

w10:297.q: With God the Father, sonship is the great relationship. With God the Supreme, achievement is the prerequisite to status—one must do something as well as be something.

w10:299: God the Father and God the Supreme (the author's summary, based on 115:0.1, 117:2.1 and 117:6.21–23)
w10:304: In the hearts of all other people
w10:305: Can be found by one person
w10:309: Where, then, do we meet the Supreme? Paper 117 answers this way.

w10:311.q: Man can discover the Father in his heart, but he will have to search for the Supreme in the hearts of all other men

w10:313: The way to the Father turns inward; the way to the Supreme turns outward, toward our neighbors. The two ways join in one great circle.

w10:315.q: His Deity is the great avenue through which the love of the Father flows outward to all creation, and he is the great avenue through which finite creatures pass inward in their quest of the Father, who is love.

w10:317: Paper 117 then shows what travels along that avenue.

w10:319.q: Man can never take the love of the Father and imprison it within his heart. The Father's love can become real to mortal man only by passing through that man's personality as he in turn bestows this love upon his fellows. The great circuit of love is from the Father, through sons to brothers, and hence to the Supreme. The love of the Father appears in the mortal personality by the ministry of the indwelling Adjuster. Such a God-knowing son reveals this love to his universe brethren, and this fraternal affection is the essence of the love of the Supreme.

w10:321: Love is not a still pond but a flowing river. The love we receive from the Father becomes ours only as we let it flow on to others. And as that flow builds up, the God of time grows.
w10:323: The great circuit of love — love that comes from the Father and passes through our neighbors to the Supreme (the author's summary, based on 117:6.10)
w10:325: This discovery does not come all at once.

w10:327.q: Men do not find the Supreme suddenly and spectacularly as an earthquake tears chasms into the rocks, but they find him slowly and patiently as a river quietly wears away the soil beneath.

w10:329: And those who walk this road are never alone.

w10:331.q: But no God-knowing mortal can ever be lonely in his journey through the cosmos, for he knows that the Father walks beside him each step of the way, while the very way that he is traversing is the presence of the Supreme.

w10:333: Within, the Father walks beside us; underfoot, the road itself is the Supreme. Paper 117 reminds us what this whole journey is a search for.

w10:335.q: Men all too often forget that God is the greatest experience in human existence. Other experiences are limited in their nature and content, but the experience of God has no limits save those of the creature's comprehension capacity, and this very experience is in itself capacity enlarging. When men search for God, they are searching for everything. When they find God, they have found everything.

w10:337: This week's study fits into a single sentence: God lives within us, and we meet Him again in our neighbors.
w10:340: **Supreme Being**: The God who grows through experience together with the universes of time and space. Standing alone, He is also called "the Supreme."
w10:341: **God-consciousness**: The experience of becoming aware of the reality of God through the indwelling spirit (103:1.6).
w10:342: **Great circuit of love**: The circle in which the Father's love flows through each person to his or her neighbors and on to the Supreme.
w10:346: True religion is a person's living experience of knowing God as Father and other people as brothers and sisters.
w10:347: Belief accepts a teaching; faith is that belief actually changing a life. When an institution hardens, the power of religion weakens.
w10:348: The Thought Adjuster is not a created being but an actual fragment of the Universal Father, an infallible compass that always points the soul toward God.
w10:349: The soul is not given at the start. It is born as a morontia reality from the relationship between mind and Adjuster, grows, and survives death.
w10:350: Mind is the ship, the Adjuster the pilot, the will the captain. The Adjuster never overrides the human will.
w10:351: Prayer does not change God; it changes us. Worship makes us more and more like the One we worship.
w10:352: The Supreme Being is God growing in time. We meet the Father within ourselves and the Supreme in our neighbors.
w10:356: Of the things you say you "believe," which ones are actually changing the way you live? In light of the distinction in Paper 101, is each of them belief or faith?
w10:357: In the picture of mind as the ship, the Adjuster as the pilot, and the will as the captain (111:1.9), what kind of captain are you right now?
w10:358: If you were to practice "each day you learn to love one more human being" (100:4.6) this week, who would that one person be, and where could you begin?
